subject: Urgent: sustained latency and 5xx spike impacting ClearPath (SLA & credits)
messages:
From: ClearPath Ops <ops@clearpath.health>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Persistent latency spike + increased 5xx rate — immediate impact to our production workflows

Ben / Monica —

We started seeing sustained elevated latency across the model endpoints (p95 ~ 2.4s vs baseline 0.6s) and a jump in 5xx error rates beginning 2027-02-04 18:00 UTC. This affected multiple tenants in our ClearPath cluster and caused retries and queued jobs to back up in our ingestion pipeline. Our SREs captured traces and attached a short summary to this thread (see attachment).

Immediate impacts: 30% degradations to downstream job throughput, visible errors in the claims ingestion flow, and customer-facing timeouts. This is material for our contract — we will need a formal remediation plan and an SLA credit calculation. Procurement is looped in on this thread; renewal discussions are on hold until remediation and commercial recourse are agreed.

Ask: Can Redwood provide an initial incident timeline and proposed corrective actions within the next 4 business hours? We also expect a proposed credit figure per the SLA so our procurement team can evaluate.

Thanks,
Maya Reddy
VP, Engineering Operations
ClearPath Health
[Attachment: slo-delta-analysis.pdf (PDF, 420KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Reddy <maya.reddy@clearpath.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Feb 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Persistent latency spike + increased 5xx rate — immediate impact to our production workflows

Maya — thanks for raising this and for the clear summary. Monica and our infra team are already triaging. Quick notes from our side:

- We see the same elevated p95 and a correlated increase in async queue latencies starting ~2027-02-04 17:42 UTC.
- Early evidence points to a shipping change in the autoscaler heuristics plus a kernel regression on a quantized kernel set that caused KV cache eviction thrashing under sustained long-context requests.
- Immediate mitigation we are shipping in the next 30 minutes: revert autoscaler tuning for the affected pool and apply a hotfix to the KV eviction guard.

We will schedule an executive bridge for 11:30 PT to run through the remediation timeline and commercial implications. Monica — can you draft the credit calc per the SLA and share an initial number on the bridge? Karthik, please prepare the condensed incident timeline and mitigation playbook.

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Success — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Note: attaching remediation map once Monica finalizes]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Reddy <maya.reddy@clearpath.health>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Feb 2027 11:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Persistent latency spike + increased 5xx rate — immediate impact to our production workflows

Maya / Team —

Thanks for the call earlier. Per the bridge, attached is our remediation map (high-level) and a preliminary credit calculation following Section 4.2 of the MSA. Highlights:

- Timeline: detection 2027-02-04 17:42 UTC, spike start 17:45, mitigation first deploy 11:00 PT on 2027-02-05. Root cause: interaction between autoscaler policy and new quantized kernels + KV eviction pattern (engineering write-up attached separately).
- Customer impact window used for credit calc: 2027-02-04 17:45 UTC through 2027-02-05 11:00 PT (observed stabilization).
- Proposed credit: 12.5% of monthly usage fees for February 2027 for the affected product routes (draft calc attached). We arrived at this by prorating the SLA shortfall against the contracted availability tiers.

Attachments: remediation-map-v1.xlsx; credit-calculation-draft.csv

We want to be collaborative here — if ClearPath has a preferred calculation methodology, we can align. Next steps: agree remediation actions and credit, sign an amendment for the month-of credit, and confirm timeline for a postmortem and follow-up quality gates.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Maya Reddy <maya.reddy@clearpath.health>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@clearpath.health>
Date: Fri, 5 Feb 2027 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Persistent latency spike + increased 5xx rate — immediate impact to our production workflows

Ben / Monica —

Appreciate the quick triage and the draft. A few notes from ClearPath:

- The operational impact was larger than initially estimated — the retry storm triggered by the timeouts caused secondary delays in downstream reconciliation jobs; our ops lead estimates ~18 hours of materially degraded throughput for the affected tenants.
- Procurement is asking for a transparent calculation that captures the downstream business impact. The 12.5% is a reasonable start, but we will need to see the math and a contractual amendment for audit.

We need the amendment and credit computation by end of day so our finance team can keep the renewal cadence intact. Also requesting a written commitment for extra monitoring (30-day elevated SLIs and a no-cost remediation engineering review) tied to the credit.

—Maya
Maya Reddy
VP, Engineering Operations
ClearPath Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Reddy <maya.reddy@clearpath.health>, Procurement <procurement@clearpath.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Feb 2027 17:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Persistent latency spike + increased 5xx rate — immediate impact to our production workflows

Maya — thank you and sorry again for the disruption. Summary and next steps from Redwood: 

1) Commercial offer: Redwood will issue a one-time credit equal to 15% of ClearPath's February 2027 bill for the affected services. We increased the draft to 15% after calibrating with engineering on the extended downstream impact you called out.

2) Contract amendment: Draft amendment (DocuSign link below) formalizes the credit and includes a clause for recordable remediation work and a post-incident engineering review at no additional cost. We will send the DocuSign by EOD for procurement sign-off.

3) Operational safeguards: 30 days of elevated SLI monitoring with weekly checkpoint calls (no charge), and a technical postmortem published within 7 business days with targeted quality gates for autoscaler and quantization kernel tests.

Links: DocuSign amendment (https://docusign.com/CLP-2024-0017/amendment-draft) | HubSpot ticket CLP-2024-0017 (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/CLP-2024-0017)

If that is acceptable, please sign the amendment and we'll schedule the postmortem review this week. If procurement needs alternate language on auditability of the calc, loop in your legal contact and we'll accommodate.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Success — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Attachments referenced earlier: remediation-map-v1.xlsx; credit-calculation-draft.csv]
